Bounded density and wave-speed pairs

Both exploratory boxes use jam density between 150 and 300 veh/mi/lane. The primary wave-speed range is 5–20 mph; the expanded range is 3–20 mph, because some saved fitted wave speeds fall below 5 mph. These are sensitivity assumptions, not universal limits or traffic-validated estimates.

Primary combinations (CSV)Expanded combinations (CSV)Compare both bounds in the summaryBounds, sources and verification
Pair selection and capacity consistency

Hold fitted discharge fixed

kj(ω)=μ0q+μ0ω

Each target queue speed defines a density–wave-speed curve. Intersect this curve with the stated parameter box and the physical speed bound. The lower and upper target-ω columns report the resulting interval when it exists.

Preserve capacity when possible

C*=vfω*kj*vf+ω*
minimize|C*−C|

Among pairs that attain the selected speed, first preserve the current capacity if possible; otherwise minimize its absolute change. If the inverse target is outside the box, reoptimize the same emission objective over the attainable speeds, then select the closest-capacity pair.

“Target reachable” means the inverse queue speed is attainable within the box; it does not guarantee an exact emission match. Capacity changes above 10% are highlighted for review, not treated as an acceptance threshold. Select the primary or expanded bounds below; each view has 137 episodes × 2 strategies.
